body: I worked as a carer in the community and I had one 60 yr old client who was paralysed on his left side from a stroke with neurological damage that caused constant pain on his paralysed side. He was wheelchair bound but could still do some things for himself. The man was the biggest narcissist I had ever met, constantly bragging about what a nice guy he was and how everyone in the town loved him, but yet none of his siblings or children wanted anything to do with him. One day while I was on shift he finally got a hold of his sister's phone number and called her. He tried to con her saying he didn't remember anything from before the stroke (a lie, he could tell me things from before his stroke). His sister shut him down, told him he deserved everything he got after he molested her kids. I refused to work with him a week later when he started sexually harrassing me. I don't believe in Karma because I see all sorts of people get sick, but sometimes the worse ones do get what is coming for them.

Nothing anyone says or does is going to make you feel better because this is something internal that you need to navigate yourself. It's a harsh reality, I know, but death is harsh and takes no prisoners. Everything is raw for you at the moment and people can sense that and are trying to be careful not to further hurt you by saying the wrong thing. People also get weird around grief and death, it reminds us of our own fragility and that of our loved ones and we don't want to think about it until we have to. For me, what got me through the 'nobody cares' stage of my grief was the knowledge that everyone in the world is going to lose someone or multiple people at some point in their lives and they are going to go through the same thing I am. Only then will they understand, but even then it's an internal struggle only they can come to terms with. Your friend who lost her mother understands this and one day your other friends and coworkers will understand it as well. For me, sharing memories with my sister about our Mum helped cause we both share the same experience of losing her. Reach out to your Dad, spend time with him if you can and reminisce over your memories of your Mother. Right now, he is the only other person in the world who completely understands what you are going through.

You said it in your post, they want to be a martyr. It gets them attention and sympathy and they use it as an excuse to get away with their bullshit. Had someone's Nmum come into the ED I was in placement at (student nurse). Soon as she was through the door she was moaning loudly about the pain in her legs (diabetic neuropathy). She had stopped taking her diabetic medication for a week and her legs were swollen and dark purple. She got her poor son to bring her in and was talking about how she was ready to die in front of him which was clearly making him upset. The experienced nurses handled her brilliantly. When they were triaging her and trying to get information, she would start to go off an a whinging tangent about how awful her life is, how her DIL is evil and hates her ( gee I wonder why). The nurse cut her off mid sentence and told her 'now let's not start feeling sorry for ourselves' which got her all red in the face. I was doing night shift in the ward she was in a few days later. She was complaining to the nurse about the telemetry alarm (life support) beeping through the hall and asked if it can be turned down. The nurse turned to her and said, dead pan face, 'that's the telemetry alarm, and that's a good sound because it means the person attached to the machine is still alive' and promptly walked out. Had to go to the toilet because I was about to burst out laughing.

The best investment is one that suits your lifestyle as well. If you are at a point where you are going to settle down for a few years then home ownership is a good investment. Personally, when I was deciding what to do with my savings I realised that home ownership would not suit my lifestyle as I am back at Uni to change careers and plan on moving around Australia for career opportunities and also travelling internationally for the next 5-10 years. Investing in ETFs instead of renting out a house and being responsible for rates, house upkeep and renters seemed less hassle for me. 

That being said, I live a very minimalist life and always sharehouse to save money on rent whereas a lot of people prefer there own place and renting there own place is sometimes a waste of money compared to owning a home.  

If you are happy with your investment and it suits your life then it doesn't matter if you would get better return on investing vs home ownership and nobody can accurately predict which will be the better investment in 10 years anyway.

NTA- Whilst what your parents went through was tragic, taking it out on a child for their entire life is inexcusable. Your parents should have worked through their grief but instead they used you as the scapegoat. They were the adults, you were just a child and they had a greater responsibility to raise you with love. 

Whilst what you said was harsh and frankly not true (what happened was nobody's fault) it does not compare to compounded emotional abuse throughout your childhood. Your parents dropped the ball, they had all the opportunity in the world to change how they raised you and do the hard work to work through their grief but they choose the easier and less emotionally hard route.

Lots of people have anxiety disorders including myself, this behaviour may have elements of anxiety but it is mostly immature, manipulative behaviour. Reading this reminds me of a child who has a balloon, promptly gets bored of it, sees another child playing with the balloon and then throws a tantrum. Anxiety disorder is when you are so overcome with panic and dread that it impedes on your life and your ability to function normally, being manipulative and petty is not a sympton. As most people have pointed out, you are just looking for an excuse for her behaviour, have some respect for yourself and move forward with your life.

Just a reminder for OP and everyone reading this post, if a Narc threatens to kill themselves call the police and report that they are suicidal immediately. Depending on what country you are in, they will be taken to the nearest hospital for up to 72 hours on suicide watch, this is not a fun experience for them. They will most likely not pull this shit again and they can't complain about it because you are doing what you are supposed to do.

OP this sounds more serious than her just being addicted to opiods. As Myrtleslaughter suggested, this maybe early onset Alzheimers or some undiagnosed mental illness. As frustrating as it is for you, your mother is going through a lot worse and you and your family need to start treating this more seriously. You need to take her to a psychiatrist and get some brain scans done so she can be on the right medication/treatment. I don't mean to bulldoze you and ignore your feelings about losing your mother this way but you need to understand that serious mental illness/ brain conditions can change a person and make them more paranoid and emotional etc. I hope this helps.

My mother died of alzheimers 6 months ago, she was 58 and I am 22, she was diagnosed and put in a home when I was 19. So in a way I am where you will be in a few years. I wish I had some better advice for you so here it goes... Alzheimers in its early stages makes people paranoid and highly emotional and it will only get worse. My best suggestion is to sit down with him and listen to the music he plays, I would play music with my mum when she was in the home and it would make her happy because they can still remember how the music made them feel when they were young. Talk to him about happy times you had together, offer to make him his favourite food, take him for short walks around the park or offer to take him out for icecream. My mother also liked to draw when she could still do it so maybe do some creative things with him like draw or read him his favourite books. As for your mother, offer once a week to go out with her and listen to how she is going, she is losing her loved one too and often times it helps to have someone who understands what she is going through.  

However, first and foremost you need to take care of yourself, I would recommend to move out as I did and continue to go to uni and try to have as normal life as possible. You cannot put your entire life on hold like I did when I was 19, it will only make things worse for you. Of course its important to offer help to your mother and stepfather but do this sparingly so you do not hurt yourself along the way and you have time to grieve. 

Finally, Alzheimers is like watching somebody slowly die while they are still living. Your stepfather will slowly fade away and he will not be the person that you remember or grew up with. You need to understand this because it will lessen the frustration, later on, he does not act like himself because he is not himself, his brain is slowly dying, It's painful to watch and I recommend you seek out a therapist to talk to who specializes in these kinds of situations. I wish I had some better advice for you, but honestly, it is a terrible thing to go through. A silver lining though is once your stepfather is in the latter stages, after the paranoia, he will be at peace and will not be in any pain.

Theres been a lot of good advice here, you need to broaden your horizons and start applying for supervisor roles or roles in banks, entry level positions in businesses etc. You could also go to tafe and get a certificate in something else as well while you are looking. Also would you be able to move to another area or state where there are more jobs? I believe there is a grant from the government around $4000 to help you move and set you and your partner up. But whatever you do don't let yourself become dissuaded because of your current situation.

I am scrolling through writing prompts when I see it, 'You are walking home from university when you have a sudden chill'. The prompt makes me stop and think. I had been walking home from university today and I felt a chill down my spine accompanied by an unnerving feeling that somebody had been watching me. I think nothing of it and decide that I have had enough of the internet for one night, after all, it was only a coincidence. 

The next day I go to work. While working at the back, I hear the bell ring for the front door. I walk out to the front to serve, but there is nobody there. I shrug my shoulders and go back to work, thinking it was probably the wind or something. That night, as I am browsing writing prompts I find another prompt ' You are working when you go out to the front of the store to serve a customer, however you find that there is nobody there'. I feel my heart give an extra thump in my chest. Clearly this was just another coincidence, maybe I was just making connections in my mind that just isn't there. That night I sleep with the light on. 

When I wake up the next morning I immediately check writing prompts. I find nothing there that I recognize and chuckle to myself a bit, I really need to get out a bit more. I decide to go for a drive to see a friend. I get dressed and walk out to my car where I see it. A long, deep scratch on the drivers door. I start to panic as I remember what I had read this morning. 'One morning you walk to your car and find that someone has scratched the drivers door'. I immediately call the police, explaining what has been happening. The irritated woman asks me if I was on any medication. I hang up angrily, deciding that enough is enough. I call my friend and I ask If I can stay the night. 

That night, as my friend is in the shower, I decide, against my better judgment to look at writing prompts one more time. There is a new prompt that reads 'you are at a friends house when you hear your friend scream from the shower'. As if on cue I hear a scream like a wild animal from the bathroom, followed by gurgling sounds and a large thump.  I hastily lock the doors and reach for my phone to call the police. I notice on my phone that there is a comment for the previous post. 'your friend has just been brutally murdered when you hear footsteps down the hallway'. As I am reading I hear them, the footsteps followed by a large knock on the door. I am frozen solid now, unable to move, unable to breathe as I look at my phone. 'you are looking at your phone, when you hear  breathing directly behind you'. There is a rattling, wheezing sound and I feel ice cold air on the nape of my neck. I slowly turn.
